nodes.name: Liquid-phase chemical synthesis
nodes.procedure: The a-HE-Se was prepared by injection of tetrahydrofuran (THF)/triethylene glycol (TEG) solution of metal and Se precursors (Ru(acac)3, Rh(acac)3, Pd(acac)2, Ir(OAc)3, Pt(acac)3 and dibenzyl diselenide) into TEG containing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as surfactant at 230°C. Diorganyl diselenides such as dibenzyl and diphenyl diselenides have been widely used in the preparation of selenide-based nanocrystals due to their high reactivity to release Se through the cleavage of C-Se/Se-Se bonds.

nodes.source_text: The catalytic activity of prepared selenides toward acidic HER was then evaluated in 1.0 M HClO4 aqueous solution. The cyclic voltammograms collected after electrochemical cleaning and before HER showed no characteristic peaks assigned to oxidation/reduction of zero-valence noble metals... The Tafel slope calculated from Figure 4a was 82 mV dec-1 for a-HE-Se... The overpotential required to reach the current density of 10 mA cm-2 is 60 mV for a-HE-Se... The mass PGM-normalized current density of a-HE-Se is 2.75 A g-1 at -0.1 V vs. RHE

nodes.source_text: The stability of the selenides toward acidic HER was investigated by chronopotentiometry measurements under 20 mA cm-2. The overpotential required by a-HE-Se increased in the beginning stage but remained stable afterward... the particle size and porous nanostructure of a-HE-Se were preserved after 20 h of the chronopotentiometry test

nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 4f, a-HE-Se exhibits significantly enhanced catalytic activity compared with c-HE-Se. The overpotential at 10 mA cm-2 was 107 mV for c-HE-Se and the current density at -0.1 V was merely one-fourth of that for a-HE-Se.
The stability of c-HE-Se is also similar to that of a-HE-Se (Figure 4d)
The Tafel slope calculated from Figure 4a was 82 mV dec-1 for a-HE-Se... comparable with Ru-Se (77 mV dec-1)
The Tafel slope calculated from Figure 4a was 82 mV dec-1 for a-HE-Se... lower than those of Rh-Se (102 mV dec-1)

The Tafel slope calculated from Figure 4a was 82 mV dec-1 for a-HE-Se... lower than those of... Pt-Se (112 mV dec-1)

The electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) of a-HE-Se and c-HE-Se was then obtained by a Cu underpotential deposition method (Figure S23). As shown, a-HE-Se showed a higher ECSA-normalized current density over the entire potential range, indicating its higher intrinsic activity.

nodes.characterization_summary: a-HE-Se nanoparticles show size of 15-20 nm with branched nanostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The size of the obtained nanoparticles (NPs) was 15 - 20 nm as determined by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: a-HE-Se shows disordered atomic arrangement confirming amorphous nature; c-HE-Se shows well-ordered atomic arrangement with interplanar distances of 0.30 nm and 0.25 nm matching (200) and (211) facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM images as presented in Figure 1b and c show the disordered atomic arrangement, indicating the amorphous nature of the prepared HE-Se NPs... Interplanar distances of 0.30 and 0.25 nm match well with the spacings between the (200) and (211) facets...

nodes.characterization_summary: Synchrotron XRD pattern of a-HE-Se shows only broad peaks consistent with amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The synchrotron XRD pattern (Figure 1d) shows only broad peaks, which is in good agreement with a noncrystalline structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic composition of a-HE-Se is Ru/Rh/Pd/Ir/Pt/Se = 6.5/6.0/6.4/6.0/5.9/69.2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic composition of Ru / Rh / Pd / Ir / Pt / Se was quantified by X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (XRF) to be 6.5 / 6.0 / 6.4 / 6.0 / 5.9 / 69.2 (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX maps show all PGM elements (Ru, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt) and Se are randomly distributed over entire a-HE-Se particles; consistent atomic ratio with XRF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A HAADF-STEM image covering several NPs is presented in Figure 1f, and the corresponding EDX maps are shown in Figure 1g-l. As can be observed, all the PGM elements and Se are randomly distributed over entire particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES first derivative maximum at 22120.9 eV indicates Ru valence ~+2.3 in a-HE-Se; PGM elements show valences +2 to +3; no edge shift in c-HE-Se.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the first maximum on the first derivative of the Ru K-edge XANES spectrum (Figure S1a and b) of a-HE-Se (22120.9 eV) was quite similar to that of Ru-Se... Linear fitting... suggests that the Ru valence is close to +2.3 in a-HE-Se

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS shows single peak at 2.08 Å assigned to Ru-Se coordination in a-HE-Se; similar M-Se coordination (~2.4 Å) maintained in c-HE-Se; no Ru-Ru (2.35 Å) or Ru-O (1.58 Å) coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In terms of the Ru K-edge EXAFS spectra (Figure 2a), the Ru foil shows a peak at 2.35 Å of the Ru-Ru coordination, whereas RuO2 shows the first peak at 1.58 Å... only one peak is observed at 2.08 Å and it can be assigned to the nearest Ru-Se coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: PDF analysis confirms amorphous structure of a-HE-Se (signal approaches zero beyond 6 Å); peaks at 2.46 Å and 3.71 Å indicate M-Se short-range order similar to crystalline RhSe2/RuSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The PDF of a-HE-Se approaches zero beyond 6 Å (Figure 2f), evidencing the absence of long-range order... Two peaks were observed at 2.46 and 3.71 Å...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XRD tracks amorphous-to-cubic phase transition of HE-Se; amorphous structure maintained up to 673 K, cubic RhSe2-like peaks appear at 773-873 K with lattice parameter a = 6.0013(7) Å (Pa-3 space group).
